By considering the interpretations and insights of rabbis and scholars, you may feel more confident in your decisions, knowing that they are grounded in a rich and time-tested tradition. On the other hand, relying too heavily on external authorities can potentially lead to a sense of disconnection from your own inner compass. This doesn't mean that you're not making decisions at all, but rather that the decisions might feel more like a reflection of the tradition, rather than a genuine expression of your own values, desires, and intentions. "How do I feel about the options available to me?" "What are my own values and priorities, and how do they align with the traditional teachings?" By engaging in this kind of introspection, you can begin to develop a more nuanced and balanced approach to decision-making, one that honors both the wisdom of tradition and the uniqueness of your own perspective. This way, you can cultivate a sense of ownership and agency in your decisions, while still drawing upon the rich resources of your heritage.
